title: Newcomer priors, multi-season blending, and an opponent-style audit
status: DEVELOPMENT-ONLY. Re-runs no frozen evaluation and judges no promotion gate. One measurement (the price prior) was shipped; the other three are negative results recorded so they are not re-opened without new evidence.
population_note: A newcomer is a player with no archive row in either of the two seasons preceding the one being predicted. Targets are the appearance rate over a season's first five observed gameweeks. Identity is `code`; club is resolved from fact rows via team_code.

a_multi_season_blend.question: Does a season t-2 term (owner proposal 0.2*t-2 + 0.3*t-1 + 0.5*last-5) help?
a_multi_season_blend.verdict: NO for appearance, YES for per-90 rates. The proposed weights lose to the shipped 0/0.7/0.3 in every position group.
a_multi_season_blend.note_on_the_bigger_error: The 0.5 on the last-five window is a larger error than the 0.2 on t-2. Fitted last-five weights run 0.148-0.432 and the repository already measures 0.7 long / 0.3 recent as optimal at a season boundary.
a_multi_season_blend.note_on_fitting: A fitted four-parameter OLS is the WORST of the six in every position group, so these weights should not be fitted; a principled fixed prior generalises better.

per_90_rates_single_triple_2023_24_to_20.caveat: xG/xA are complete only from 2023-24, so exactly one (t-2, t-1, t) triple exists and the MAE figures are in-sample. Indicative, not conclusive.
per_90_rates_single_triple_2023_24_to_20.pooled_trap: The pooled ALL row reads 0.864 for xg90 and must be ignored: it reproduces the documented 0.871 pooled-across-position artefact.

injury_return_cohort.definition: appearance >= 0.70 in t-2 and <= 0.30 in t-1

current_model_bias.reading: The current model DOES under-rate this cohort, significantly.

injury_return_cohort.reading: More weight on t-2 is worse even on the cohort it targets. The cohort is a mixture -- 47% barely play again, 9% become nailed -- and two-season-old statistics cannot say which branch a given player is on. That information is current availability, which belongs in the overlay.

b_club_positional_median.question: For a newcomer, is his club's positional median a better base than a league prior?
b_club_positional_median.verdict: NO. The club dimension adds nothing; the apparent gain is a level correction.

paired_club_median_minus_newcomer_base.reading: Not significant. Whatever the club median gains, a position-level newcomer base rate gains too.

c_price_prior.question: Does launch price separate newcomers the model currently cannot tell apart?

degeneracy_measured_on_the_live_gw1_run.example: Twelve zero-history midfielders at one club span 1.349-1.508 expected points with prices 4.5m and 5.0m interleaved through the ordering -- Monte-Carlo noise from each player's own draw stream, not information.
degeneracy_measured_on_the_live_gw1_run.does_ev_vary_by_opponent: Yes. Zero-history defenders span 0.822-1.868 across clubs, because Stage A is opponent-aware. Only the WITHIN club-and-position ordering is noise.

c_price_prior.known_weakness: Defenders gain nothing (-0.2%) and their signed bias worsens from +0.075 to +0.130. They ship on the same rule anyway; dropping them after seeing that number would select a rule on its own test set.

d_opponent_style_audit.question: Does opponent playing style add anything beyond opponent strength, at team or player grain?
d_opponent_style_audit.verdict: NO at both grains. Do not ingest an external style feed on this evidence.
d_opponent_style_audit.method_note: Deliberately generous: style indices were built from the FULL season (hindsight) and scored in-sample. A signal that cannot survive here cannot survive point-in-time.
style_proxies: control = negated z-score of xGC allowed per match

team_grain.reading: The raw spread is huge (1.808 against 1.154) and the strength model absorbs all of it. Style and strength are collinear -- good teams control, weak teams absorb.

player_grain_split_half.measure: a player's xG+xA per 90 against absorbing opponents minus against controlling opponents, computed on his odd matches versus his even matches

pooled_all.warning: IGNORE. Pooling positions reproduces the documented pooled-across-position artefact; only the within-position rows are meaningful.

d_opponent_style_audit.data_availability: mart_fact_team_match carries goals, team_xg, team_xgc, team_bps and fdr only. Possession, passes and shot counts are absent from the FPL archive. FBref via the existing operator-pull recipe (docs/phase3-stage-c-fbref-recipe.md) is the established route if this is ever re-opened, and its column mapping is unverified until the 2025-26 overlap gate passes.

e_price_prior_impact_on_gw1.note: Both forecasts generated at as_of 2026-08-21T17:30:00Z on the same database; the pre-change run was produced by checking out the parent commit.

spillover_to_players_with_history.cause: attacking shares are normalised across a club's squad and bonus is simulated jointly per fixture (one winner), so an opponent's cold start moves you too

in: Rulli (5.0m GK, 0.0% owned, no PL history)

identified_risk.name: the prior is absolute, not club-relative
identified_risk.detail: A mid-priced newcomer behind a dearer incumbent at the same club is over-rated. Rulli at 5.0m reaches the 0.85 cap and outscores Man City's 5.5m Donnarumma (4.83 against 3.82) despite 0.0% ownership, and that inversion drove the squad change above.
identified_risk.not_verifiable_here: Manchester City play in GW1 fixture 8, which had not kicked off when the last committed snapshot was captured, so Rulli's actual GW1 outcome cannot be checked from committed data.
identified_risk.candidate_fix_not_implemented: Ownership (selected_by_percent) is loaded and unused, and would rank two keepers at one club. That is a modelling change needing its own validation window, so it is recorded here rather than patched in.

f_club_relative_cap.question: Can the absolute price prior's blind spot to a club's existing starter be closed without fitting anything new?
f_club_relative_cap.verdict: YES for the decision failure, at a small distributional cost. SHIPPED as BEHIND_INCUMBENT_CAP.

measured_group.definition: newcomer whose club fields a same-position team-mate with eligible history and a prior-season appearance rate of at least 0.70
measured_group.replication: 0.284 over the 201 historical rows and 0.283 over the 98 of them in 2025-26.
measured_group.reading: The middle row is nearly exact and the outer two are compressed toward it. The cap addresses only the bottom row.

f_club_relative_cap.design: A ceiling at the measured 0.284, never a floor. It adds no fitted parameter and consumes no validation window. The job resolves the dearest established same-position team-mate in a pre-pass over the deadline registry.

effect_on_gw1.motivating_case: Rulli, 5.0m goalkeeper, 0.0% owned, no PL history: 1.380 before any prior, 4.825 under the price prior, 1.587 with the cap -- now below his club's incumbent Donnarumma at 3.822.
effect_on_gw1.honest_trade: The cap wins MAE overall and on the cold-start subset, and loses slightly on mean log score and CRPS. Capping at a group MEAN truncates the upper half of that group, which also deepens the existing under-prediction of cold starts. Both variants beat no prior on every metric. On 359 rows over six fixtures none of these differences is individually significant -- the actual total alone carries an 8.9% standard error -- so this is a decision-safety choice, not a measured accuracy win.

expensive_and_widely_selected_vs_expensi.note: Prices are near-identical between the two high-price groups (5.75m against 5.22m), so this is not a price effect. Ownership at both price levels also separates (cheap: 0.354 against 0.138).

why_not_built: Three ownership encodings were tried against the live 2026/27 GW1 window, which spends it: log-odds floored at 0.001% (+18.0%, t=-4.97, but a cliff at the 0.0/0.1% rounding boundary), floored at 0.05% (+14.9%, t=-3.85, but the goalkeeper correction disappears), and a within-position percentile (+10.8%, t=-4.77, stable surface). Those figures are optimistically biased by that iteration.

Goalkeepers cannot express the effect at all: 39 training rows where price already separates almost perfectly leave the ownership term inert in every encoding, so the very case that motivated the work is the one it cannot fix.
An additive three-feature model (price + relative price + ownership) reached only t=-1.59 on the strict 2025-26 holdout and regressed in three of four positions.
ownership_deliberately_deferred.confirmation_window: 2026/27 GW2 onward, untouched by any fit or holdout in this record.
